transcript.text: When a vacuum stops working completely, it is usually due to a simple power interruption or a safety cut-out tripping. To narrow this down quickly: is your vacuum corded or cordless? If it is corded, please check that the plug is securely in the wall socket and that the fuse hasn't blown (if you are unsure, try a different appliance in that socket to confirm the power is on). If it is cordless, has the battery been charged for at least 30 minutes?
its corded. the lamp works in the socket so its not that. it cut out when i was doing the stairs

Since the power is confirmed at the socket, the fact that it cut out while you were using it suggests a safety mechanism has triggered or an internal fault occurred. Most corded vacuums have a thermal cut-out that trips if the motor overheats or becomes blocked; this often happens on stairs where airflow can be restricted. Please look for a reset button (usually red) on the body or near the dust bin, press it, and try switching the vacuum on again. If it still doesn't work, we need to check for internal damage from the strain of carrying it up the stairs. To help me guide you further, what is the make and model number of your vacuum?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

its a Henry, the red one with the smiley face. cant read the label, cant turn it over with my back. theres no red button that i can see. the wire has some tape on it near the plug and once it came on for a second when i moved it

The fact it flickered on for a second when you moved it strongly suggests an intermittent electrical fault in the power supply path. Given the tape near the plug and the strain of carrying it up stairs, the most likely cause is a broken wire inside the flex or a loose connection at the plug. Please unplug the vacuum first. Inspect the taped area carefully for any cuts, exposed copper wires, or soft spots in the rubber. Gently wiggle the cable there and near the plug; if you see any damage or feel it moving loosely inside the insulation, that is your fault. If the cable looks fine externally, please check where the cord enters the back of the vacuum body for any cracks or looseness. If you find visible damage to the cable or plug, do not use it—this is a fire and shock hazard. You will need to replace the flex or plug (a qualified electrician or appliance repair person can do this safely). If the cable looks perfect but it still won't start after cooling down for an hour, we may be looking at an internal switch failure.
i'm not wiggling it again, it frightened me. the tape is a bit bent near the plug. i haven't got a screwdriver or spare fuse either. should i just leave it unplugged?

Yes, please leave it unplugged. Given the bent tape near the plug and the fact it only flickered on when moved, there is likely an internal break in the wire that poses a shock or fire risk if used again. Since you cannot safely inspect or replace the cable yourself (no tools, back issues), I recommend contacting Numatic directly or a local appliance repair service to replace the flex or plug for you.
